summary: Disc-derived yellow N game icon and interrupted-setup recovery.
body:
Nitrogen Squared 0.2.2 — development candidate

First setup
SDL and framework revision checks now run with their own closed input, tracked processes and a 30-second deadline. Stop can cancel these checks. Setup logs identify each command, exit code and failing command, and Git downloads report progress.

The clean Windows first-setup stall is still under investigation; this candidate needs Windows CI and owner testing. Local synthetic checks do not establish that the reported Windows stall is fixed.

Keep your entire .local folder. Completed tools, imports, settings and saves are retained. Compatible 0.2.0/0.2.1 game builds remain reusable; game code, native coverage and clocks are unchanged.

Updating from 0.1.x
The older updater rejects the new launcher notice directory. Download the complete Windows package and replace its files manually, preserving .local. This candidate cannot change updater code already installed in an old release.

Interrupted setup recovery
If Git initialization finishes but setup stops before origin is added, the next attempt now adds the expected source remote before fetching. Existing empty source folders can resume too. SDL and framework preparation share this repair; an existing different origin or populated revision is preserved and reported. The full Windows setup still needs owner verification.

Private game icon
The compiled game now uses the yellow N icon decoded from your verified disc. Its PNG, multi-size ICO and build receipt stay under .local. Windows embeds the icon in the private executable; the game window uses the same image. This requires one build update, preserving saves/settings and completed preparation. Later compatible launches reuse the result. Game logic, clocks and native selection are unchanged. Icon appearance still needs Windows player verification.
